content.value_statement: IdeaVim documentation can drift from Kotlin APIs and recent commits. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through targeted verification and documentation updates.
actual_capabilities: Finds IdeaVim documentation in doc/, README.md, and CONTRIBUTING.md.
Searches Kotlin implementations and real examples before judging documentation accuracy.
Compares documented function signatures, parameters, and usage patterns with current APIs.
Uses git history and diffs to identify removed or renamed behavior.
Updates inaccurate documentation while preserving existing style and useful context.
Reports checked files, discrepancies, updates, and items needing human review.
limitations: It is tailored to the IdeaVim repository and its documentation layout.
It needs access to the relevant code, docs, and git history for best results.
It does not prove runtime behavior unless the user asks to run tests separately.
Ambiguous product behavior may still require maintainer review.

use_cases.title: Validate Documentation After API Changes
use_cases.description: Check whether changed Kotlin APIs require updates in docs or README examples.

use_cases.title: Audit Existing Code Examples
use_cases.description: Compare documented examples with working implementations before publishing a release.

use_cases.title: Review Contribution Impact
use_cases.description: Identify documentation affected by a pull request before it is merged.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Documentation File
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner verification of a single file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether doc/ideavim-mappings.md matches the current IdeaVim code. Report any inaccurate examples and update only confirmed issues.

prompt_templates.title: Review Code Changes For Docs
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review after a focused implementation change.
prompt_templates.prompt: I changed MappingScope.kt. Inspect the recent diff, find related documentation, and update examples that no longer match the current API.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Recent Breaking Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review recent removal or deprecation commits and identify documentation that still references removed functions, parameters, or files.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Release Documentation Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Check all documentation in doc/ for API examples that differ from current working implementations. Prioritize critical inaccuracies and summarize unresolved questions.

output_examples.input: Check doc/ideavim-mappings.md against current mapping APIs.
output_examples.output: The report lists the documentation file, the Kotlin API files checked, each mismatch found, and the exact documentation updates made.

output_examples.input: I changed MappingScope.kt. Do docs need updates?
output_examples.output: The response identifies related documentation, explains whether examples still compile conceptually, and records any edits or maintainer review notes.

output_examples.input: Audit the doc folder before release.
output_examples.output: The output groups checked files, confirmed discrepancies, completed documentation fixes, and lower-confidence items that need human confirmation.

best_practices: Start from working code examples before deciding that documentation is correct.
Verify every documented function name, parameter name, and usage pattern against the current API.
Make small documentation edits that directly address confirmed code and documentation drift.
anti_patterns: Do not update documentation based only on preferred wording or style changes.
Do not trust documentation examples without checking real implementations.
Do not remove helpful context unless the current code proves it is wrong.

faq.question: What repository is this skill designed for?
faq.answer: It is designed for the JetBrains IdeaVim repository and its documentation layout.

faq.question: Can it edit documentation files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can update documentation when it confirms that examples, paths, or API details are outdated.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on documentation verification unless the user separately asks to run tests.

faq.question: Why does it inspect git history?
faq.answer: Git history helps identify removed, deprecated, or renamed behavior that documentation may still mention.

faq.question: Can it check a single file?
faq.answer: Yes. It can verify one documentation file against the relevant code and examples.

faq.question: What tools does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects file reading, editing, search, glob, and local shell access for read-only git or search commands.
